title: Installation
text: setupmjr is distributed as a compiled Go CLI. Use the native package path where available, the release installers when you want a user-local binary, or build from source.

title: Installation
text:
Ubuntu / Debian

APT repository
Configure the published apt-miguelrodo repository once:
sudo apt-get install -y curl gpg
curl -fsSL https://miguelrodo.github.io/apt-miguelrodo/KEY.gpg \
  | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/apt-miguelrodo.gpg
echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/apt-miguelrodo.gpg] https://miguelrodo.github.io/apt-miguelrodo stable main" \
  | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/apt-miguelrodo.list >/dev/null
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y setupmjr
The Debian package depends on bash and repos, so APT resolves those dependencies through the repository.

title: Installation
text:
macOS

Homebrew
The GitHub repository MiguelRodo/homebrew-tap is the Homebrew tap MiguelRodo/tap:
brew tap MiguelRodo/tap
brew trust MiguelRodo/tap
brew install MiguelRodo/tap/setupmjr
Homebrew 6 requires explicit trust for non-official taps. The setupmjr formula depends on MiguelRodo/tap/repos, so trusting the tap allows Homebrew to resolve that dependency automatically.

title: Installation
text:
Linux / macOS user-local installer
For a no-sudo release installation on Linux or macOS:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
bash install-local.sh
The installer downloads the latest release binary, verifies it against checksums.txt when SHA-256 tooling is available, and writes to the first writable directory already on PATH. If none is writable, it falls back to ~/.local/bin and prints the required PATH instruction. If repos is missing, the installed binary runs setupmjr install --repos.
The installer supports both amd64 and arm64 release binaries.
To uninstall an installation recorded by this installer:
bash uninstall-local.sh

title: Installation
text:
Windows

Scoop
scoop bucket add MiguelRodo https://github.com/MiguelRodo/scoop-bucket
scoop install setupmjr
The published Scoop manifest declares repos as a dependency.


Installer script
Alternatively:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
.\install.ps1
The script downloads the latest release binary into the first writable directory already on Path. If repos is missing, it runs setupmjr install --repos and fails if that dependency installation fails.
To uninstall the recorded installation:
.\install.ps1 -Uninstall

title: Installation
text:
From source
With Go installed:
go install github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/cmd/setupmjr@latest
Or build a local clone:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
go build -o setupmjr ./cmd/setupmjr

title: Installation
text:
Coding-agent CLIs
Install the terminal applications independently of provider selection:
setupmjr install agents
This installs Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot in order, skipping each CLI already found on PATH. Each agent gets a completion, skip or error result. If an installation fails, the command still attempts the remaining agents and returns an error listing the failures. It does not update already-installed CLIs; ensure their installation directories are on PATH before running it again.
To run an individual installer instead:
setupmjr install claude
setupmjr install codex
setupmjr install copilot
These are subcommands, not combinable flags. They delegate to the same vendors’ supported installers, whether run individually or via agents; they do not sign in, change API credentials, set a model provider, or modify existing agent configuration. Use setupmjr agent --config to inspect configuration.








CLI
Linux, macOS and WSL
Native Windows




Claude Code
Anthropic native install.sh via Bash
winget install --id Anthropic.ClaudeCode --exact --source winget


Codex
OpenAI native install.sh via sh
OpenAI native install.ps1 via Windows PowerShell


GitHub Copilot
GitHub’s gh.io/copilot-install script via Bash
winget install --id GitHub.Copilot --exact --source winget



On Windows, install WinGet before the Claude and Copilot commands if it is absent. On Unix-like hosts, Bash is required for Claude and Copilot; Codex requires sh. No Node.js installation is required for these paths. On WSL, run the Linux setupmjr executable to install Linux CLIs, not the Windows executable.
For scripts, setupmjr uses a bounded download into a temporary file and executes it only after a complete download. This avoids partial-download execution, but the scripts are still mutable third-party code without a pinned checksum; review the vendors’ installer sources if that trust model is inappropriate for your environment. Native package managers handle their own validation and elevation prompts. Installers may use the network and request additional system dependencies.
After installation, start a fresh terminal if the CLI was added to your PATH. Run setupmjr agent doctor for read-only installation, local authentication and managed-configuration diagnostics (see agent diagnostics), or check versions individually:
claude --version
codex --version
copilot --version
Then authenticate using each CLI’s own flow, for example claude, codex login or copilot followed by /login. None of the setupmjr install subcommands handles authentication.
Official references: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI.
Update installed agents with setupmjr agent update <claude|codex|copilot> or setupmjr agent update --all. See agent updates for supported installation methods, platform details and per-tool results.

title: Installation
text:
Managed components
The top-level install command owns installation glue for external tools:
setupmjr install --repos
setupmjr install --pj
setupmjr install --gh-skill
Flags may be combined. Regardless of flag order, setupmjr runs --repos, then --gh-skill, then --pj, and stops at the first failure:
setupmjr install --repos --gh-skill --pj

--repos installs the latest released MiguelRodo/repos binary into ~/.local/bin; use repos directly afterwards.
--gh-skill installs github-projects from MiguelRodo/github-projects-skill for universal agents at user scope from main.
--pj installs or updates the launcher from MiguelRodo/pj using its floating v0 release line.

At least one target flag is required.

title: Installation
Installation
text:
Verify installation
setupmjr --version
setupmjr --help

title: git
text: The git subcommand configures Git identity and GitHub authentication.

title: git
text:
Commands
git
git profile
git auth [text|cache|mngr] [--system|--local] [--remove]

title: git
text:
Default setup
setupmjr git
This fills in missing Git name/email values and then configures GitHub authentication.
setupmjr git auth prefers a durable GitHub CLI login. If gh auth login has already authenticated github.com, setupmjr runs gh auth setup-git --hostname github.com. Otherwise it uses the protected-token fallback described below.
The persistent-login check deliberately ignores GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, so an environment-only token is not mistaken for a durable GitHub CLI login.

title: git
text:
Scope and replacement
Authentication configuration is global by default. Use --system or --local to select another Git config scope:
setupmjr git auth --local
--remove clears existing credential helpers in the selected scope before setupmjr configures the requested authentication path:
setupmjr git auth --local --remove
Use one scope flag for clarity. If both --system and --local are supplied, the current CLI selects --system.

title: git
git
text:
Migration
Current authentication setup removes active legacy GH_TOKEN= and GITHUB_USERNAME= assignments written by older setupmjr versions. It also migrates the short-lived managed block that older versions could place directly in .bashrc or .zshrc into the corresponding login.sh file.

title: git
text:
Consumers
Both authentication paths use Git’s standard credential interface. That is the integration boundary for command-line Git, R gitcreds and VS Code Dev Containers’ credential forwarding.
For Remote SSH → HPC → Dev Container workflows, configure authentication on the host first. If a container cannot reuse the helper, treat that as a forwarding problem rather than copying a PAT into devcontainer.json, a Dockerfile, an image or a repository file.

title: git
text:
Legacy explicit helpers
These older explicit helpers remain available but are not part of the default authentication path:
setupmjr git auth cache
setupmjr git auth mngr

title: shell
text: The shell subcommand configures Bash or Zsh startup files. setupmjr bash is shorthand for setupmjr shell bash.

title: shell
text:
Commands
shell <shell> rc.d
shell <shell> path
shell <shell> login [--not-profile]

bash rc.d
bash path
bash login [--not-profile]

title: shell
text:
rc.d
setupmjr shell bash rc.d
setupmjr shell zsh rc.d
This ensures ~/.<shell>rc.d exists and configures ~/.<shell>rc to source readable files from that directory.

title: shell
text:
Details
The sourcing loop is:
for i in $HOME/.<shell>rc.d/*; do [ -r "$i" ] && source "$i"; done

title: shell
text:
path
setupmjr shell bash path
setupmjr shell zsh path
This first ensures the shell’s rc.d directory is wired in, then installs path-executables.sh there so ~/bin and ~/.local/bin are available on PATH without duplicating entries.

title: shell
text:
login
setupmjr shell bash login
setupmjr shell zsh login
This installs login.sh in the shell’s rc.d directory and configures the corresponding login profile to source the directory. Bash uses ~/.profile unless ~/.bash_profile already exists; Zsh uses ~/.zprofile.
Use --not-profile when you want the login.sh file but do not want setupmjr to modify the login profile:
setupmjr shell bash login --not-profile

title: r
text: The r subcommand configures R-related user and project files.

title: r
text:
Command
r [--not-radian] [--not-lintr] [--switch-r]
Running:
setupmjr r
configures the user-level radian and lintr defaults.

Flags

--not-radian skips the ~/.radian_profile configuration.
--not-lintr skips the ~/.lintr configuration.
--switch-r adds the project-local scripts/r/switch_r.R helper and ensures the current repository’s .Rprofile sources it.

For example:
setupmjr r --not-lintr
setupmjr r --switch-r
The HPC command accepts the same R flags:
setupmjr hpc r --not-lintr

title: r
text:
Details
Unless --not-radian is supplied, setupmjr ensures ~/.radian_profile contains:
options(radian.auto_match = FALSE)
Unless --not-lintr is supplied, setupmjr ensures ~/.lintr contains:
linters: linters_with_defaults(
    object_length_linter = NULL,
    object_name_linter = NULL)
With --switch-r, setupmjr creates scripts/r/switch_r.R if it is absent and places this source line at the top of the current repository’s .Rprofile:
try(source("scripts/r/switch_r.R"))

title: setupmjr
text: setupmjr is a cross-platform setup utility for shell, R, Git, repository, HPC and coding-agent environments.

title: setupmjr
text:
Start here
Install the CLI using a supported package manager, release installer or source build. See Installation for the canonical commands.
For authoritative top-level syntax, run:
setupmjr --help
The agent command also has detailed option help:
setupmjr agent --help

title: setupmjr
text:
Command groups







Command
Purpose




setupmjr hpc
Configure Linux HPC shell, Git, scratch, Apptainer, SLURM and R setup.


setupmjr shell
Configure Bash or Zsh startup, executable paths and login integration.


setupmjr bash
Shorthand for setupmjr shell bash.


setupmjr r
Configure radian, lintr and the optional project-local switch_r helper.


setupmjr git
Configure Git identity and GitHub authentication.


setupmjr repo
Scaffold repository files, devcontainers and released workflow examples.


setupmjr install
Install or refresh external tools whose setup glue is owned by setupmjr.


setupmjr agent
Configure coding-agent credentials, providers and opt-in subagents.



External tools keep ownership of their own behaviour. In particular, use repos directly after setupmjr install --repos, and use pj directly after setupmjr install --pj.

Guides

Installation
HPC

title: repo
text: The repo subcommand configures the current repository. Repository orchestration itself belongs to the standalone repos CLI.

title: repo
text:
Commands
repo readme
repo devcontainer [--repo <owner/repo>@<branch>] [--build]
repo action <action-name>

title: repo
text:
repo readme
setupmjr repo readme
Interactively scaffold a standard README.md with title, purpose, contacts, links and details sections.

title: repo
text:
repo devcontainer
setupmjr repo devcontainer
setupmjr repo devcontainer --repo MiguelRodo/comp@main

--repo selects the source repository and branch in <owner/repo>@<branch> form. The default is MiguelRodo/comp@main.
--build also installs the prebuild-devcontainer.yml workflow example from the latest published MiguelRodo/actions release.

The source archive is staged before extraction, and repository/branch values are passed as command arguments rather than interpolated into shell commands.

title: repo
text:
repo action
setupmjr repo action <action-name>
Workflow examples are owned by MiguelRodo/actions. setupmjr resolves its latest published release and installs examples/<action-name>.yml from that exact tag into .github/workflows/.
Use the released example filename without the .yml suffix. setupmjr keeps no embedded workflow copies and does not fall back to mutable actions/main; a missing released example is an error.

title: repo
text:
repos CLI
Install or update the standalone repository-orchestration CLI with:
setupmjr install --repos
Then use repos directly. setupmjr owns its installation glue, not its commands.
Network downloads used by these setup paths have finite timeouts and are staged before replacing final files, so failed or incomplete downloads do not become installed artefacts.

title: agent
text:
Use setupmjr agent for user-level coding-agent configuration. pj launches already-configured agents; provider and credential setup belongs here.
Install all three CLIs with setupmjr install agents (see installation). It uses the existing native vendor installers, skips CLIs already on PATH, and leaves authentication, API credentials and configured model providers unchanged.
Run setupmjr agent --help for authoritative option syntax and setupmjr agent --list for accepted endpoints, providers, subagents and aliases.

title: agent
text:
Inspect configuration
setupmjr agent --config
setupmjr agent --list
--config reports the effective Codex provider, Copilot provider and configured opt-in subagent. Running setupmjr agent without options prints command help.

title: agent
text:
Update installed CLIs
setupmjr agent update claude
setupmjr agent update codex
setupmjr agent update copilot
setupmjr agent update --all
Choose one agent or --all; these selectors cannot be combined with provider or authentication options. Updates use the first matching executable on PATH. With --all, missing tools are reported as skipped; a missing single selection is an error. Every installed tool is attempted even if another fails, with a separate completion or failure line for each tool and a nonzero exit status if any failed. Vendor output reports whether a version changed or was already current; completion means the update command succeeded.







Installed method
Update path




Native Claude, Codex or Copilot on Linux, macOS, WSL or Windows
The installed CLI’s update command, after checking its help advertises that command


Homebrew executable resolving into Caskroom or Cellar
brew upgrade --cask <installed-package> or brew upgrade --formula <installed-package>


Claude or Copilot resolving into a Windows WinGet package directory
winget upgrade --id <installed-package> --exact --source winget


Detected npm/shim, system /usr/bin or /bin, or Nix installation
Report an error directing you to the original package manager



Homebrew package suffixes and Copilot’s WinGet prerelease package are retained. An installed package manager must be on PATH. Other custom wrappers or install layouts may not reveal their package manager; native update support and installation handling are then delegated to the vendor. Older CLIs without an advertised update command require a one-time update through their original installer or package manager. setupmjr does not automatically migrate them to another installation method.
An explicit update requests a manual check even when background updates are available. Existing auto-update settings, environment variables and release-channel configuration are passed through. setupmjr does not rewrite provider configuration, sign-in state, credentials or shell startup files. Vendor updaters may use the network, request permissions, and require running agent sessions to be restarted. On WSL, use the Linux setupmjr and Linux agents. Platforms other than Linux, macOS and Windows are rejected.
See the official Claude update documentation, Codex command reference, and Copilot command reference.

title: agent
text:
Diagnose installations
setupmjr agent doctor
Doctor checks Claude Code (claude), Codex (codex) and GitHub Copilot CLI (copilot) on the current process’s PATH. It prints the selected executable locations, versions and setupmjr-managed provider/subagent configuration, then continues through all checks with actionable fixes. It exits 0 when no checks fail and 1 when any check fails, including a missing CLI. WARN means unverified and does not change the exit status. Extra options are rejected; doctor cannot be combined with setup actions.
Checks are read-only: doctor never installs, updates, signs in, sources shell files or writes configuration. It invokes only --version, Claude’s auth status and Codex’s login status, with closed stdin and a ten-second timeout per probe. Raw command output and errors are suppressed; only version numbers and credential-presence/status summaries are displayed. It makes no inference requests or deliberate credential-validation network requests. Local credential presence does not establish validity, account entitlement or service connectivity.
Copilot authentication may live in an OS credential store. Doctor does not inspect that store or launch an interactive session: it reports authentication as unverified when no token environment variable is available. It checks COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN in precedence order for empty values and unsupported classic PATs, without printing their values. Provider API keys are reported as present but unvalidated. To resolve access problems, run copilot login yourself.
Managed DeepSeek checks detect missing credentials, an inactive Copilot shell environment and incomplete isolated subagent configuration. An opted-in agy subagent must be on PATH; its authentication remains unverified. CODEX_HOME is honored by the Codex checks and produces a warning because it can override setupmjr’s configuration in ~/.codex. Custom providers, CLI-specific configuration overrides and credential helpers may need separate investigation.
Platform details:

Ubuntu/Linux and WSL: PATH checks describe the current Linux environment. A Windows installation does not establish that the Linux CLI is available in WSL; run the Linux setupmjr executable there.
macOS: the same CLI status commands support credentials stored through vendor mechanisms, including Keychain; doctor does not assume that a missing plaintext credential file means signed out.
Native Windows: lookup uses Windows PATH/PATHEXT. Doctor probes native executables directly; .cmd/.bat shims produce an actionable failure asking for the native installation. Claude Code needs Git for Windows (Git Bash). Bash/Zsh exports do not configure PowerShell; configure custom provider variables in the shell that launches Copilot.

title: agent
text:
Store DeepSeek authentication
setupmjr agent --auth deepseek
setupmjr agent -a d
Authentication is credential-only: it does not change the active Codex or Copilot provider.
setupmjr reuses DEEPSEEK_API_KEY when available, then checks its managed credential and existing Codex DeepSeek configuration, and otherwise prompts without echoing the key. The reusable credential is stored at:
~/.config/setupmjr/agent/auth/deepseek.key
The file is private and can be reused by both managed DeepSeek provider paths. DeepSeek is currently the only managed --auth endpoint.

title: agent
text:
Copilot provider
GitHub-managed Copilot models are the default value for -p:
setupmjr agent -p
setupmjr agent -p g
setupmjr agent --copilot-provider github
Switch to DeepSeek after storing its credential:
setupmjr agent --auth deepseek
setupmjr agent -p d
The managed environment lives at ~/.config/setupmjr/agent/copilot.env and is sourced by Bash and Zsh startup files. DeepSeek uses its Anthropic-compatible endpoint with the Flash model; COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic selects the wire protocol, not Anthropic as the model vendor.
The raw key is not embedded in the provider environment. Switching back to github removes the managed BYOK provider variables for new shells. Restart the shell, or source the managed environment file, after switching. GitHub authentication for Copilot remains separate from provider selection.

title: agent
text:
Codex provider
OpenAI/ChatGPT is the default value for -c:
setupmjr agent -c
setupmjr agent -c o
setupmjr agent --codex-provider openai
Switch to DeepSeek with:
setupmjr agent -c d
setupmjr agent --codex-provider deepseek
The first managed DeepSeek setup uses DeepSeek’s official Codex setup script and selects the Flash model. setupmjr stages that script with its bounded downloader and runs it with bash --noprofile --norc plus a reduced environment. A timeout, failed HTTP response or incomplete download prevents execution.
This remains a remote-code trust boundary: DeepSeek publishes the installer at a mutable CDN URL without a versioned script or checksum that setupmjr can pin. If you do not want to run the vendor script, use DeepSeek’s documented manual Codex setup instead: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/agent_integrations/codex/.
Before provider changes, setupmjr snapshots the active Codex config.toml and models.json under:
~/.config/setupmjr/agent/codex/
After both providers have been seen once, switching restores local snapshots instead of rerunning the DeepSeek installer. A pre-existing manual DeepSeek installation uses the vendor restore path once to capture the OpenAI state.
Provider changes affect the ordinary ~/.codex home. Restart active Codex clients after switching. Restoring OpenAI configuration does not itself restore a ChatGPT login that a previous DeepSeek session may have displaced.
The automated DeepSeek bootstrap requires Bash and is intended for Linux, macOS and WSL.

title: agent
text:
Opt-in subagent
agy is the default value for -s:
setupmjr agent -s
setupmjr agent -s agy
setupmjr agent --subagent agy
This installs bounded Codex guidance for explicitly authorised delegation through agy, preserving instructions outside the managed block.
DeepSeek can be configured instead:
setupmjr agent -s deepseek
The DeepSeek subagent uses the isolated Codex home ~/.codex-deepseek-subagent and does not change the primary Codex provider. Its worker runs through codex exec --sandbox workspace-write. Delegation remains opt-in for the current task or conversation.
Selecting one managed subagent replaces the other. --subagent-agy remains as a deprecated compatibility alias for --subagent agy.

title: agent
text:
Credential boundaries
setupmjr creates managed agent-state directories with mode 0700 and credential/snapshot files with mode 0600 on POSIX systems. DeepSeek’s Codex config.toml format contains the API key, so DeepSeek snapshots are credentials too. Do not commit or share the managed credential or snapshot files.

title: hpc
text: The hpc subcommand configures Linux HPC environments.

title: hpc
text:
Commands
hpc
hpc scratch
hpc apptainer
hpc slurm
hpc git
hpc r [--not-radian] [--not-lintr] [--switch-r]
Install setupmjr using a supported Linux method from Installation, then verify it with setupmjr --version.

title: hpc
text:
Master setup
setupmjr hpc
The master command is Linux-only and stops on the first failed step. It runs:

Bash rc.d, executable-path and login/profile setup.
Zsh rc.d, executable-path and login/profile setup.
Git identity and GitHub authentication.
HPC scratch configuration.
Apptainer helpers.
SLURM helpers.
Normal setupmjr r defaults.

The focused subcommands below run the same components independently.

title: hpc
text:
Git
setupmjr hpc git
This is the normal setupmjr git setup. It prefers a persistent GitHub CLI login and otherwise uses setupmjr’s protected-token credential helper. See Git for authentication, migration and Dev Container behaviour.

title: hpc
text:
Scratch space
setupmjr hpc scratch
This installs ~/.bashrc.d/hpc-scratch.sh, which points large caches and artefacts at /scratch/$USER when available, including Apptainer/Singularity storage and R library/renv caches.
The master setup wires Bash rc.d first. When running hpc scratch independently, run setupmjr shell bash rc.d first if Bash is not already sourcing ~/.bashrc.d.

title: hpc
text:
Apptainer
setupmjr hpc apptainer
This installs the embedded apptainer-* helper scripts into ~/.local/bin, excluding apptainer-vscode.

title: hpc
hpc
text:
R
setupmjr hpc r
This delegates to the normal R setup and accepts the same flags:
setupmjr hpc r --not-lintr
setupmjr hpc r --switch-r
See R setup for the flag behaviour.
